thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER DUTY: High error rate detected for inference-usw pool - multiple kubelet restarts observed on a subset of GPU nodes. Severity: P1. Paging oncall.
oncall-bot: Incident runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/infra/infer-node-flap (auto-attached)
pagerduty: Paging kelly.h, aj for oncall rotation (incident triggered at 2025-10-12T03:10:56Z).
kelly.h: I'm on it. seeing alerts: kubelet restart x3 on hosts infer-usw-gpu-23..25, nodes toggling NotReady. CPU fine, but pods failing with OOM / container crashloop for the serving runtime.
aj: I can take networking/routing. assigning myself to reroute traffic.
kelly.h: quick tl;dr from node logs: kernel messages show GPU driver fault around same time, then kubelet panicked and restarted. container logs show repeated: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory" and then liveness probe failing.
ryan.m: are these nodes part of the dedicated pool or shared?
kelly.h: these are in the us-west inference pool (shared), some dedicated customers pinned to variants on these nodes. impact: 10% increase in 5xx and token latencies doubled for ~7% of requests.
lina: customer impact: CS flagged two customers (acme-corp, beta-ai) with elevated errors. I've opened a bridge and notified CS.
aj: immediate mitigation: I'll update smart-routing to avoid us-west for non-regulated traffic and direct to eu-central fallback. Pushing routing override now.
aj: command run: 
```
# add routing policy to prefer eu-central for infer-usw pool fallback
redwoodctl routing set --from inference-usw --to inference-euc --weight 0.9 --until 2025-10-12T04:00:00Z
```
kelly.h: good. also cordon the flapping nodes and trigger a rolling drain to let scheduler move pods and avoid restarts. Doing cordon+drain on 23,24,25.
kelly.h: commands: 
```
kubectl cordon infer-usw-gpu-23
kubectl drain infer-usw-gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
```
sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step executed: cordon-and-drain started by kelly.h. Next step: collect kernel oops and dmesg, capture /var/log/messages, and check driver version.
kelly.h: pulling dmesg, looks like nvidia-driver 535.86.10 threw a GPU fault around 03:09:45, followed by container OOMs. attaching sample log snippet: 
```
[03:09:45] NVRM: Xid (0001) at 0x... GPU fault: perf counter overflow
serving.runtime: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 128MB
```
lina: can we rollback any recent driver or kernel updates? change history shows a node image rollout last night touching a small subset.
kelly.h: yes there was a focused kernel/driver bump in us-west pool last night. I'm escalating to infra to evaluate rollback. filing infra ticket INC-4591.
aj: routing override is live, monitoring metrics. latency for the bulk of traffic is back to baseline, error rate for impacted customers still elevated until retries expire.
ryan.m: what about autoscaling? can we spin up fresh nodes in us-west with older driver profile to drain into?
kelly.h: good idea. launching a small set of new nodes with driver pinned to 535.54.03 via infra self-service. If those come up healthy we can shift load back.
kelly.h: started node bootstrap at 03:22. nodes booting.
sre-runbook-bot: Next recommended action: if driver rollback is required, coordinate with infra and schedule a rolling replace.
lina: CS updated customers: temporary region fallback in place, investigating root cause, ETA 1h.
aj: monitoring shows drop in 5xx back to baseline for non-pinned traffic. tagging incident as partial mitigation: traffic rerouted + drains in progress.
kelly.h: once nodes are drained I'll run a controlled restart of kubelet on one node to verify stability on new image.
kelly.h: kubelet restart test on infer-usw-gpu-26: passed, no OOMs after restart.
kelly.h: nodes 23-25 still in NotReady during drain, driver faults present. infra says rollback of driver is happening now.
ryan.m: after rollback and nodes back Ready, we should run a canary routing to move 10% back to us-west and watch for errors for 15m.
aj: agreed, I'll prepare the canary policy.
kelly.h: updating incident timeline and notes in ops doc. escalation to infra ongoing.
oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial. paging suppressed. Keep channel updated.
lina: handoff to next oncall at 04:00 UTC: aj will take lead, kelly.h staying on infra coordination.
aj: acknowledged, taking over. continuing monitoring and will run canary after infra confirms rollback completion.
kelly.h: final note, root cause likely driver/compat mismatch combined with runtime memory regression in the new model quantization path. will open a follow-up ticket for runtime team to add additional OOM guards.
ryan.m: thanks all — CS to follow up with customers once fully resolved.
aufinish: reaction :thumbsup:
